issue: When the victim is Indian, is the defendant's Indian or non-Indian status under the intra-Indian carve-out of 18 U.S.C. § 1152 an essential element the government must allege and prove, or an affirmative defense the defendant must raise?

sides.position: The defendant's Indian/non-Indian status is not an essential element. It is an affirmative defense the defendant must properly raise, after which the government keeps the ultimate burden of proof.
cases: United States v. Hester, 719 F.2d 1041, 1043 (9th Cir. 1983)

sides.position: Both the victim's and the defendant's Indian/non-Indian status are essential elements. The government must allege them and bear the burden of production and persuasion at trial.
cases: United States v. Prentiss, 256 F.3d 971, 975-80 (10th Cir. 2001) (en banc)

quote: A circuit split exists on this issue.
cite: United States v. Haggerty, 997 F.3d 292 (5th Cir. 2021)
